_status: INACTIVE SYNTHETIC TEMPLATE. No authorization or prior execution is transferred. Configure recipient resources and obtain explicit authority before live use.
classifier: seren_harness/cli_errors.py at the commit recording version 2: a token-refresh HTTP failure (Unexpected Response or Error Response) is category unknown, rule token_refresh_http_error, stage token_refresh, with no HTTP status; communication failures are network_failure and payload failures malformed_response; conflicting signatures are unknown.
purpose: Establish whether the dedicated fixture can be read from the stated execution environment, and if not, record a fixed, source-backed failure category. Follows preview diagnostic 1, whose two prerequisite reads exited 1 after about 6 ms each with no retained cause.

target.name: Seren Harness Test
target.config: ~/seren-harness-live/config.json (private; existing Seren CLI OAuth session by reference)

baseline.last_observed: Inactive synthetic handover example. Recipient must establish a fresh baseline and authorization.

correction.use: only to check whether the read shows the recorded original instruction (a boolean); nothing is previewed or sent

limits.basis: Pinned v0.10.0: managed_agent_get builds the client (cli/src/command_context.rs client -> commands/auth.rs get_bearer_token, which refreshes the OAuth token only when the stored token is near expiry: at most one token request, redirects disabled), then sends one GET. The SDK client (sdk/src/lib.rs from_config) uses reqwest's default redirect policy (up to 10 redirects) and has no retry logic, so the GET is one request plus any redirects: at most 12 HTTP requests, normally 1 or 2. The 60 s harness timeout kills and reaps the CLI process. One CLI invocation is therefore not guaranteed to be one HTTP request.

execution_environment.host: Inactive synthetic handover example. Recipient must establish a fresh baseline and authorization.
execution_environment.executable: the config's seren.executable, pinned by seren.executable_sha256 ddf617c4… (CLI 0.10.0); checked locally before the call; no substitute binary
execution_environment.credentials: the Seren CLI's stored OAuth session for profile default, under the CLI's own config directory (cli/src/config.rs config_root/profile_dir). Used only by the CLI; never read, copied or inspected by the harness. No API key, new login or refresh is requested by the procedure; the CLI may refresh by itself near expiry.
known: Preview diagnostic 1 ran from the agent's shell tool and both reads exited 1 after about 6 ms; the cause was not retained.
Recipient must establish and record a fresh successful read before dependent operations.

On every invocation the pinned CLI creates its config directories if missing and sets them to mode 0700 (config_root/profile_dir), and saves the session after a refresh, so it needs write access to its own config directory, not only read access.
unknown: whether the agent's shell tool restricts network or file access for child processes (no sandbox setting in the user's Claude settings files; other policy sources not checked)
whether the stored OAuth session is currently valid; it is not inspected
execution_environment.choice: The owner states, when authorizing, where the command runs: (a) the agent's shell tool, as before, or (b) the owner's own shell, for example by typing `! <command>` in the session. The procedure does not move execution between environments by itself.

evidence.kept_on_success: deployment matches target, identity and revision match the baseline (booleans), active_revision_id (UUID only), detail status (allowlisted enum), approval applied (boolean), instruction is the original or the corrected text (booleans), conditions by allowlisted type and state
evidence.kept_on_failure: a fixed classification: category, rule identifier, stage, HTTP status only when parsed from the CLI's own 'unexpected response <code>' format, and source-backed booleans before_main_request / http_response_received (null when not established)
evidence.never_kept: the response, config, secret_keys, stderr, messages, paths, URLs, headers, tokens or any hash of them

stop_conditions: local pins, CLI checksum or version differ: refused before any call
a recorded journal whose inputs differ: refused before any call, journal untouched
after the one read (any outcome, including timeout or interruption): stop; it is never resent
excluded: No cloud deployment status, preview, update, provisioning, Passwords action, start, stop, login, credential repair, Discord request, probe or model session. A successful read ends the task; any further step needs its own decision and authorization.
acceptance: Either result read_matches_fixture / read_differs_from_fixture with the safe projection, or result not_read with a fixed failure category (possibly unknown) and its stated uncertainty.
